_notes: pregame_gate (default true; only the boolean true turns it on): on a fresh start the bot checks that the loaded table is arranged for a new game (definition in sparring/table_reset.py) and shows three buttons on the right panel: 'Limpiar mesa' (destroys every hero and map on the table, the leftovers of the save, and creates the discard zones), 'Preparar' (reads the map and the two heroes the player dragged from the roster, the bot's on the +x half and the player's on the -x half, closed bag or opened; says what it detected; lays the map at its calibrated transform and every hero object at its slot; it refuses, with a chat line, a hero it cannot play, a missing or repeated hero, two heroes on one half or no map) and 'Comenzar partida' (only when the table is ready: reads the heroes and the map and runs the normal start). false starts at once, as before. Never applies to --resume.

layout: the DEFAULT slots the pre-game gate leaves each side's objects in (an uncalibrated map uses them as they are), one slot (pos x y z, rot x y z) per ROLE and side, read from Ivan's hand-arranged table (TS_AutoSave 5/11 09:37) and mapped to the GUIDs of whatever hero sits on that side through data/tts/<slug>.json (sparring/table_layout.py). A calibrated map brings its own layout and deck spots from config/map_setups.json (sparring/map_setup.py; write it with `python -m sparring.calibrate --map <key>`, never by hand). Roles: deck, character_card (taken out of the deck, 31 -> 30), dial (the first fighter with a life dial), sidekick_dials (the other fighters' dials in order), counter_dials (destiny...), tokens (the hero's special tokens), pieces (the fighters' miniatures/tokens in order). A hero with more objects than slots keeps the extras where they were unpacked and the chat says so. Objects are laid 0.2 above the y given so that TTS drops them. bot_deck_spot / human_deck_spot must stay at the deck slot (the deck is found within deck_radius of them; a calibrated map sets them from its deck slots). The human deck slot (-6.7, 17.55) touches the corner of the human discard zone (x up to -6.98, z up to 17.2): its centre is outside by about 0.3.

language: language of the panel and the chat, "es" (default) or "en" (one data/i18n/<code>.json file per language; a missing tag falls back to Spanish); --language overrides it. Card and hero names stay as printed. With --resume the language the game was saved in is used again, unless --language is given explicitly (then lines already saved, such as ability_wait or the applied lines of a combat, may stay in the old language).

ongoing_hold: seconds the bot pings your ONGOING scheme on its zone, after saying why it left play, before moving it to your discard pile itself; 0 skips the pause. If the table cannot do it you are asked to move it by hand.

wildfire_hold: seconds the bot (playing Liz) leaves the bottom card that Wildfire discards in view, face up on its discard pile, before applying its effect; 0 turns it off and applies it at once. The wait happens inside TTS, in the same message.

action_announce_hold: seconds between the chat notice of what the bot is about to do (maneuver, attack, scheme, ability, resolution of its combat) and the writes on the table; 0 turns it off and the notice comes afterwards, as before. In fast mode the wait goes inside the same TTS script (lua.hold). wildfire_hold and ongoing_hold are the same pause for those two scenes, with their own duration.

bot_pause: seconds of pause after each bot action (and before your turn) so the table does not move all at once; 0 turns it off; --bot-pause overrides it. It is a Python sleep: it costs no TTS messages.

bot_hero / human_hero: slug of data/heroes/<slug>.json of each side (medusa, hellboy, abe-sapien, baba-yaga, liz-sherman, leonardo, donatello, michelangelo, raphael, doctor-strange, houdini, bigfoot, daredevil, luke-cage, bullseye, golden-bat, jill-trent, she-hulk or tomoe-gozen; not the same on both sides: their GUIDs would be the same). "auto" (or the key missing) = the bot detects it at start-up by reading the table: a hero is present if there is a loose Deck or Card with a CardID of its range (data/tts/<slug>.json, deck.card_ids; what is inside bags does not count) AND, for decks, by the deck image identity (deck.identity, see docs/card-identity.md: several heroes share CardID ranges, so the range alone does not tell them apart) and it belongs to the side whose bot_deck_spot / human_deck_spot is closest; if it is unclear, it refuses to start and says so. Priority: --bot-hero / --human-hero > value written here > detection (with --resume, the saved game wins over detection). If the table cannot be read, it falls back to medusa / hellboy with a warning. What this key leaves out, the configuration can override by hand (pieces, dials, nicknames, bot_deck_guid, human_deck_guid, destiny_dial), but with another pair of heroes it is normally better not to write it.

Official save (Unmatched Official Tournament Table October 2026 (Hellboy)) set-up, done by the bot at start-up. discard_zone_rot_y / bot_discard_zone_spawn / human_discard_zone_spawn: if the discard zone GUID in bot_discard_zone / human_discard_zone is not on the table (the official save has no such zones), the bot first adopts a Scripting zone already on the table whose position and scale match this transform within 1.5 (any GUID, any rotation: one an earlier run created and never saved), and only otherwise creates a Scripting zone there with this position and scale (TTS gives it a new GUID, which the bot uses for the session and keeps in its state file, never in this file), and rotation (0, discard_zone_rot_y, 0); a zone that IS on the table (the hand-made 906a7a / b7a0b8 of the pre-sparring save) is only straightened to that same rotation. 270 puts the long side along z; the zones of the pre-sparring save were slightly crooked (269.09 / 269.43) and are now straight. Leave a *_spawn key out to turn that zone's creation and straightening off. bot_discard_bounds must describe the bot zone as created (center x, center z, size x, size z, rotY): tests check it against bot_discard_zone_spawn. Position y 4.1422 and height 5.1 are the ones of the pre-sparring save.

remove_table / remove_table_limits: loose objects of the official save (and of the pre-sparring table, which has the two clocks too) that the bot does not want on the table, as GUID -> expected TTS object name: DeckCustom addeca and cb6cbc (78 cards each, in the centre where the B.P.R.D. HQ board goes), Die_20 65be8d, the locked Custom_Assetbundle Dice Cannon 5085eb and the two Digital_Clock 6126d5 and 790396. On a fresh start (never with --resume) each one is DESTROYED, and the bot says so in the chat, only if all of these hold: an object with that GUID is on the table, its TTS name is the expected one (TTS can hand a freed GUID to another object: the Timers bag 3bcddb holds a Digital_Clock template with GUID 790396), it lies inside |x| <= remove_table_limits[0] and |z| <= remove_table_limits[1] (the central table: the objects are at |x| <= 5.7 and z -30..27.2; the hands sit at |x| 30 and the hero bags past |z| 37), and the GUID is none the bot uses (zones, decks, pieces, dials). Whatever fails is left alone and reported in the chat. Nothing is ever removed by area or type, so everything else stays: the hand cards counters (d26d8c White, 5c7e75 Green), the hand and scripting zones, the fog of war trigger, the table board 45c723. Leave remove_table out or empty and nothing is removed.

TABLE values read from the real table (TS_AutoSave 27/10 09:29). The remaining TODOs are read live with --read-only. What belongs to each HERO (miniature GUIDs, dials, deck, tokens, CardID range, deck identity, names) is no longer written here: it comes from data/tts/<slug>.json.

board_guid ec6f27 (Custom_Board 'B.P.R.D. HQ'). human_seat White (HandTrigger dd569b at -30.1,-9.0); bot_seat Green (HandTrigger f8d527 at 30.0,-9.0). The ScriptingTriggers 742715 and 6ec8d9 sit over those hand zones: they are NOT discard zones (D1).

Discard zones created by the user: human_discard_zone b7a0b8 (center -12.5,0.7, ~x -18..-7) and bot_discard_zone 906a7a (center 15.0,0.7, ~x 10.75..19.25). They are big on purpose: the discard is left IN ORDER and spread over a grid so the rival can see what was played (bot_discard_spot = origin, bot_discard_step = (column dx, row dz), bot_discard_rows slots per column; slots less than 3 from the draw deck are skipped).

The draw decks are inside or at the edge of those zones: bot_deck_guid d42056 at (11.5, 12.0) (inside 906a7a) and human_deck_guid 00dc9a at (-7.7, 12.5) (edge of b7a0b8). read_discard excludes them by GUID and by position (1.5).

Deck zones (optional, absent on purpose until you create them): bot_deck_zone / human_deck_zone = GUID of a Scripting zone placed over each draw pile (TTS Zones > Scripting, a rectangle a bit bigger than a card, over bot_deck_spot / human_deck_spot, away from the discard and hand zones; right-click it to copy its GUID). When set, that side's deck (or its last loose card) is looked for ONLY inside the zone, whatever its GUID, and whatever lies in the zone is never read as discard. Without them the bot adopts the deck GUID found at start-up (and on --resume if the saved one is gone) and takes the nearest face-down deck or card within deck_radius (default 2.9, always below the 3.0 that keeps discard slots away from the deck) of bot_deck_spot / human_deck_spot. If the deck is not found the message says where it looked.

Combat zone (face-down card), according to the user: to the RIGHT of the board from the White seat, -z side, away from the dials and decks (z 12..17). human_card_spot (-2.0, -22.0) and bot_card_spot (6.0, 1.7, -22.0): between the two discard zones in x (-18..-7 and 10.75..19.25) and past the edge of the board (the anchor points reach z -13); they sit at z -22 (boxes z -23.6..-20.4) so the boxes do not overlap the right edge of bigger maps such as B.P.R.D. HQ and Naglfar (they were at z -18 until 6/11). The ONGOING boxes are 5 further, at z -27. Configurable. off_board_dist 4.0 is an estimate: calibrate it with the distances from --read-only.

start_spaces: REAL starting spaces of the table (Medusa on 30, Hellboy on 3); they are not those of the default map. bot_discard_bounds: (center x, center z, size x, size z, rotY) of zone 906a7a read from the save (live.json 27/10): the discard grid only uses slots whose center falls inside and, when full, stacks on top starting from the first. panel_position: above the playmats (y 1.0) and the objects (~1.57).

dead_spot: where the bot sets aside its fallen miniatures (one per piece, 1.5 apart in x, growing toward the table centre so Clean table reaches every one); it is an estimate, calibrate it live. human_dead_spot is the same for the human's.

Setup: the bot deals its hand, decides on a mulligan (once: the 5 cards back to the deck, shuffled and 5 dealt; house rule or unconfirmed, see the README) and places Medusa and the Harpies according to who goes first; the human places Hellboy and Lobster and presses Ready. The starting spaces come from the rulebook (the first player takes space 1 of the map, the second space 2) unless start_spaces is fixed by hand. mulligan_bot=false turns it off for the bot; mulligan_human=false turns off the human's Mulligan button.

Row of the human's cards that look at the bot's hand (Remove A Painful Memory, Advanced Psychometry, Every Possible Angle): bot_row_spot is the CENTER of the row where the bot lays its cards face up and bot_row_step the (dx, dz) between cards (2.6 in z, cards turned 90 degrees; look_rot_y turns them too). Default [11.5, 2.5, -29.0]: a column in z -20..-38 with 7 cards, to the right of the bot's combat (x 4.9..7.1) and ONGOING boxes, past the -z edge of its discard zone 906a7a (x 10.7..19.3, z -17..18) and before the hero bags (z -40) and the die (2.1, -30); free in the 26/10 save. Start-up warns if it overlaps the panel, a combat/ONGOING box or a discard. The Look at bot's hand panel button still uses look_spot.

Looking at the bot's hand (F16, panel button): look_spot is the CENTER of the row where the bot lays its cards face up (an estimate, calibrate it live: in front of the human's seat, outside the hands, discards and combat zones; start-up warns if it overlaps the panel or a combat box) and look_step the (dx, dz) between cards (2.6 in z for cards turned 90 degrees; up to 12 cards). look_rot_y (optional) turns the cards; default bot_discard_rot_y.

unpack (optional, off): with --unpack or "unpack": true (only the boolean true) the bot, BEFORE playing and never with --resume, takes out of each hero's inner bag whatever is not on the table (no GUID of its states; a deck, in addition, with no Deck or Card of its CardID range anywhere on the table) and lays it in a row from bot_unpack_spot / human_unpack_spot (default [22,2.5,-10] and [-22,2.5,10.5], outside the hand zones; each unpack_step [0,0,3]); the deck goes to its deck spot and is shuffled. If the inner bag is not on the table it does nothing and warns; it never takes from an infinite bag. start_spaces accepts fighter ids or the keys bot / human.

bot_tuck_spot / bot_removed_spot (Donatello, estimates: calibrate live): where the bot lays the inventions it tucks under its hero card and the cards it removes from the game, face up. Defaults [18,1.7,-24] and [18,1.7,-28]: two rows growing in +x (1.6 per card), past the bot_row_spot look column (x up to 13.1), beyond the -z edge of its discard zone (z -17), clear of its combat and ONGOING boxes (z -23.6..-20.4 and -28.6..-25.4) and of dead_spot (z -20; its cards reach z -21.6, the tuck row z -22.4). Start-up warns if either row (6 cards) overlaps the panel, a combat/ONGOING box, a discard, a look row or the other. Without them the bot only says what to move and you move it. The human tucks and sets aside by hand.

reveal_display / reveal_spot / reveal_scale / reveal_step (Ivan, 2026-11-08, every hero): a card text that says reveal means every player sees the cards. The bot lays a LARGE copy of each revealed card side by side (centre of the row at reveal_spot [x, y, z], size reveal_scale, reveal_step apart along z, rotation of card_zoom_rot) and they stay until the human presses the panel button Stop revealing; a new reveal replaces them. The spot is an estimate (above the zoom copy): calibrate it live.

card_zoom: when true (default) the bot shows a BIG copy of the card the human must read, like Alt+hover but triggered by it: its combat card when it is revealed (or discarded without a flip), its schemes (glance, frenzy, scheme) as they leave its hand, its ONGOING scheme placed face up and the card Wildfire discards. The copy is spawned in the same TTS message as the write, floats at card_zoom_spot, is locked and not interactable, and destroys itself after card_zoom_seconds; only one at a time. It is a Card with its own CardID (99900+) and the name SparringZoom: no read of the table takes it for a card. --no-card-zoom turns it off for a run. card_zoom_scale is the size factor (4 = four times a card), card_zoom_spot (x, y, z) must stay outside every zone (the default floats 12 above the board centre), card_zoom_rot (optional, x y z degrees) defaults to flat with the same turn as the look row (look_rot_y or bot_discard_rot_y), readable from the human seat; add an x tilt to lean it toward the camera. Estimates: calibrate live.
